about: The golden fixture for a member-rostered conversation: its handle, the envelope
that hides which conversation a sealed byte belongs to, and the group policy
Written by an independent implementation (Python's hashlib and cryptography), so
the Rust replay is a second opinion and not the author checking itself.
Replayed through the fixture door (kind "roster") in Rust, JavaScript and Swift
(and, in Peachy's Android client, Kotlin). See docs/delivery.md §Handles and sender-addressed delivery.
A judge case's leaf is an actor id or {actor, device, accountKey, deviceKey}; `kept` and `reader`, when present, feed the one-account-key rule, judged after the group's policy.

Envelope versions: version 2 (padded) is keyed by the group id, and is what a seat ask and a link preview are sealed as; version 3 is the padded layout keyed by one epoch's envelope secret (`epochSecretHex` / `epochSecretsHex`), what everything else is sealed as. A `seal` case with no `epochSecretHex` seals version 2. Any other version byte is refused (docs/delivery.md §The wrapped envelope).
A reseat compares actor, device and account key; the same device under another deviceKey is still a reseat to the policy, and the adder and every receiver refuse it on their own.

A judge case judges the commit as its committer and every receiver do. A meta that names no readable policy is a group with no admin, each unreadable part closed. No meta at all (a call link's group) is not judged.

cases.why: Version 1 (unpadded, keyed by the group id) is not a version a reader opens, even for the group it was sealed for.
A version 2 envelope relabelled 3: the group id's keys never open a version 3 envelope, and no epoch secret is held.

Version 3: the version 2 layout, keyed by one epoch's envelope secret (MLS-Exporter("peachy envelope epoch v1", group id, 32)), enc = SHA-256("peachy epoch envelope v1" || secret), route = SHA-256("peachy epoch route v1" || secret). No group id goes in.
A reader tries the epoch secrets it holds: the one the envelope was sealed under opens it.
A removed member keeps the group id and no later epoch: a version 3 envelope neither routes nor opens for it.
The version byte is in the AAD and picks the keys: a version 3 envelope relabelled 2 opens under neither.
